nodes.label: landlord notifies the tenant of the rent increase for the next possible termination date
nodes.why: The landlord may increase rent for the next possible termination date but must notify the tenant on a canton-approved form and state the reasons.

nodes.label: determine whether the rent-increase notification uses the prescribed form
nodes.why: A rent increase must be notified on a canton-approved form and is void if the prescribed form is not used.

nodes.label: rent increase is void for failure to use the prescribed form
nodes.why: The proposition expressly makes a rent increase void where the landlord does not notify it using the prescribed form.

nodes.label: tenant challenges the rent increase before the conciliation authority as abusive
nodes.why: The tenant may challenge an abusive rent increase before the conciliation authority, and the procedure is initiated by a conciliation request.

nodes.label: determine whether the tenant challenged within 30 days after communication
nodes.why: The challenge of a rent increase must be made within 30 days after it is communicated to the tenant.

nodes.label: challenge was not made within the stated 30-day period
nodes.why: The propositions state the 30-day period for making the challenge but do not state a further consequence of expiry.

nodes.label: determine whether the increase is generally not abusive under a stated Article 269a ground
nodes.why: The listed propositions identify circumstances in which rent is generally not abusive, including customary comparable rents and specified justifications.

nodes.label: conciliation authority attempts to reconcile the parties in informal negotiations
nodes.why: The conciliation authority must attempt informal reconciliation and seek an agreement covering the entire tenancy.

nodes.label: record settlement, acknowledgment of claim, or unconditional withdrawal of claim
nodes.why: Where agreement is reached, the conciliation authority must record the matter, obtain signatures, and provide each party a copy.

nodes.label: record lack of agreement and issue authorization to sue to the landlord
nodes.why: If no agreement is reached in a challenged rent-increase matter, the authority must record that fact and issue authorization to sue to the landlord or lessor.

nodes.label: landlord files action with the court under the authorization to sue
nodes.why: The authorization entitles its holder to file an action with the court, and the action period is 30 days in residential and commercial lease disputes.

nodes.label: court establishes the facts ex officio in the rent-protection dispute
nodes.why: Protection against abusive rent is within Article 243 paragraph 2 matters, for which the court must establish the facts ex officio.

transitions.condition: the prescribed form was not used
the prescribed form was used and the tenant challenges the increase as abusive
the challenge was not made within 30 days after communication
the challenge was made within 30 days after communication
the landlord files within the applicable action period

deadlines.period: at least ten days before the beginning of the notice period
deadlines.runs_from: before the beginning of the notice period
after the rent increase has been communicated to the tenant
receipt of the application or completion of the exchange of written submissions
after the opening of the authorization to bring an action

obligations.statement: Notify the tenant of the rent increase on a form approved by the canton and state the reasons for it.
Provide the notification and reasons at least ten days before the beginning of the notice period.

State the previous rent and ancillary-cost charge, the new rent and ancillary-cost charge, the effective date, and the reason for the increase; separately state each asserted increase reason as an amount.

State whether the landlord receives subsidies for value-enhancing improvements where additional services are asserted, and include statutory contestation requirements plus the list and local jurisdiction of conciliation authorities.
Justify the rent by cost increases or additional services provided by the landlord if relying on that stated non-abusive ground.
Attempt to reconcile the parties in informal negotiations and seek an agreement covering the entire tenancy.
Record the settlement, acknowledgment of claim, or unconditional withdrawal in the minutes and have the parties sign it.
Record the lack of agreement in the minutes and issue an authorization to sue to the landlord or lessor in a challenged rent-increase matter.

unsupported_gaps.what_is_missing: A stated legal consequence for defects in the required rent-increase form other than failure to use the prescribed form.
unsupported_gaps.why_it_matters: The sources expressly make non-use of the prescribed form void, but do not state whether omissions or inaccuracies in the Article 19 form content also make the increase void.

unsupported_gaps.what_is_missing: The substantive standard in Article 269 for deciding whether a rent increase is abusive, and the consequence of a finding that the increase is abusive.
unsupported_gaps.why_it_matters: Article 270b permits a challenge as abusive under Articles 269 and 269a, but only Article 269a grounds are supplied and no proposition states the remedy following an abusive-increase finding.

unsupported_gaps.what_is_missing: A stated outcome after the court establishes the facts.
unsupported_gaps.why_it_matters: The propositions require ex officio fact-finding but do not state the court's resulting decision or its effect on the challenged rent increase.

scope: a tenant challenging a rent increase imposed by the landlord, including whether the increase is void for defect of form
